title: Every department
prompt: Show every column for every row in the departments table.
hint: SELECT * returns all columns.
solution: SELECT * FROM departments;

title: Employee names
prompt: List the first_name and last_name of every employee.
hint: Name the columns you want, separated by commas.
solution: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM employees;

title: High earners
prompt: Find employees who earn more than 100000. Show first_name, last_name and salary.
hint: Filter rows with WHERE salary > ...
solution: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > 100000;

title: Highest salary first
prompt: List every employee's first_name and salary, sorted from the highest salary to the lowest.
hint: ORDER BY sorts ascending by default. Add DESC.
solution: SELECT first_name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC;

title: Top 3 salaries
prompt: Show the first_name and salary of the 3 highest-paid employees, highest first.
hint: Sort first, then use LIMIT.
solution: SELECT first_name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Office locations
prompt: List each department location once (no duplicates).
hint: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows.
solution: SELECT DISTINCT location FROM departments;

title: New York departments
prompt: Show the name of every department located in 'New York'.
hint: Text values go in single quotes: WHERE location = 'New York'.
solution: SELECT name FROM departments WHERE location = 'New York';

title: Hired in 2020 or 2021
prompt: Show the first_name and hire_date of employees hired between 2020-01-01 and 2021-12-31 (inclusive). Dates are stored as 'YYYY-MM-DD' text.
hint: BETWEEN includes both ends. ISO date text sorts correctly as text.
solution: SELECT first_name, hire_date FROM employees WHERE hire_date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2021-12-31';

title: Desk products
prompt: Show the name and price of every product whose name contains the word 'Desk'.
hint: % matches any number of characters: LIKE '%Desk%'.
solution: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%Desk%';

title: Missing emails
prompt: Find employees with no email on file. Show first_name and last_name.
hint: = NULL never matches anything. Use IS NULL.
solution: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM employees WHERE email IS NULL;

title: Orders in progress
prompt: Show the order_id and status of every order whose status is 'shipped' or 'pending'.
hint: WHERE status IN ('a', 'b') is shorter than two ORs.
solution: SELECT order_id, status FROM orders WHERE status IN ('shipped', 'pending');

title: Headcount
prompt: How many employees are there? Return a single number.
hint: COUNT(*) counts rows.
solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees;

title: Products per category
prompt: For each product category, show the category and how many products are in it.
hint: GROUP BY category, then COUNT(*).
solution: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products GROUP BY category;

title: Average salary by department
prompt: For each dept_id in the employees table, show the dept_id and the average salary rounded to 2 decimal places. Employees without a department form their own group.
hint: ROUND(AVG(salary), 2). GROUP BY puts all NULLs into one group.
solution: SELECT dept_id, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id;

title: Departments with more than 2 people
prompt: Show the dept_id and employee count for every department that has more than 2 employees.
hint: WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters groups after.
solution: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY dept_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;

title: Employees and their departments
prompt: Show each employee's first_name next to the name of their department. Leave out employees with no department.
hint: INNER JOIN departments ON employees.dept_id = departments.dept_id. An INNER JOIN drops rows with no match.
solution: SELECT e.first_name, d.name AS department FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id;

title: Headcount for every department
prompt: Show every department name and how many employees it has, including departments with 0 employees.
hint: Start FROM departments and LEFT JOIN employees. COUNT(e.emp_id) ignores NULLs, so empty departments get 0.
solution: SELECT d.name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS employee_count FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.name;

title: Customers with no orders
prompt: Show the name of every customer who has never placed an order.
hint: LEFT JOIN orders and keep the rows where the order side IS NULL. NOT IN or NOT EXISTS also work.
solution: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

title: Total spend per customer
prompt: For each customer who has placed at least one order, show their name and the total amount spent across all their orders (quantity x price), whatever the order status.
hint: Join customers, orders and products, then SUM(o.quantity * p.price) grouped by customer.
solution: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.quantity * p.price) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = o.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name;

title: Above-average salaries
prompt: Show the first_name and salary of employees who earn more than the average salary of all employees.
hint: Aggregates can't go straight into WHERE. Compare against (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees).
solution: SELECT first_name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);

title: Salary bands
prompt: Show every employee's first_name and a salary band: 'High' for 100000 or more, 'Medium' for 70000 to 99999, and 'Low' for anything below 70000.
hint: CASE WHEN ... THEN ... WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END. Conditions are checked top to bottom.
solution: SELECT first_name, CASE WHEN salary >= 100000 THEN 'High' WHEN salary >= 70000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS band FROM employees;

title: Most common order status
prompt: Count the orders for each status. Show status and count, most common status first.
hint: GROUP BY status, then ORDER BY the count DESC.
solution: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY order_count DESC;

title: Who reports to whom
prompt: For every employee who has a manager, show the employee's first_name and their manager's first_name (both come from the employees table).
hint: Join employees to itself with two aliases: employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id.
solution: SELECT e.first_name AS employee, m.first_name AS manager FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id;
